moments.label: He said to them, “Don’t be amazed. You seek Jesus, the Nazarene, who has been crucified. H

glossa.source_pressure: The Greek verb is ἠγέρθη — a MARKED aorist passive (the passivum divinum, God the unspoken agent). Mark had active options (ἤγειρεν 'he raised him', ἀνέστη 'he rose'), so the passive was a choice, not a necessity.
glossa.rendering_choice: Each version decides what to do with a theological load already on the verb: Latin surrexit (ACTIVE — partly language-forced, resurgo has no passive); KJV 'is risen' (stative be-perfect); WEB 'has risen' (eventive have-perfect).
glossa.formal_consequence: A passive → active → stative → eventive drift; and the announcement fuses to one move in Latin, atomizes to four in the KJV.
glossa.interpretive_stakes: God's act (passive) vs Jesus's own act (active) — but the theology is MARK's, encoded in the 1st-century Greek, not the translators'. They inherit the load and decide what to carry.
glossa.citation: Thayer s.v. ἐγείρω; Lewis & Short s.v. resurgo; panel verdict (RESITUATE_translation_panel_pilot_readable_s161)
